**Visual analysis of test image:**
- Multiple soybean plants collapsed/dead in a central cluster, surrounded by healthy green plants
- Brown, dried stems visible at/near soil level
- Plants at trifoliate leaf stage — past seedling, but young
- Characteristic "damping-off" patch pattern with lodged dead tissue

**Key observations matching candidates:**
- The Pythium damping-off reference shows very early-stage rotted seeds/hypocotyls — doesn't match the more developed plants here
- The Rhizoctonia reference (bottom-right panel) shows multiple plants collapsed with brown stem rot at soil line — closely matches the test image pattern of localized plant death with brown stems and surrounding healthy plants

Rhizoctonia root rot/hypocotyl rot is the best fit: it causes collar rot/canker lesions at the soil line in more developed seedlings, resulting in the observed lodging/collapse pattern in patches.
